title: Why do people stockpile
titleChinese: 人们为什么要抢购囤货？
paragraphs: Have you ever watched one of the many TV shows set during the apocalypse - a dystopian future where life as we know it is over and people are only focussed on survival? If it’s not zombies, it’s viruses or natural disasters. One thing that seems to be a quintessential part of these series is survivors searching for food and resources. Is that why people stockpile food when things go bad?

What is stockpiling? Quite simply it’s when people accumulate a substantial number of goods, for example food or water. According to psychologist Judy Rosenberg, stockpiling perishable goods like eggs and milk is a positive sign that people believe a crisis will be over soon. When people stockpile tinned goods, it can be a sign that people fear that the crisis will endure.

But why do we do it? Consumer psychologist Paul Marsden puts it down to three factors that relate to retail therapy. Firstly, ‘autonomy’ – the idea the people feel the need to be in control. Secondly, ‘relatedness’ – panic shopping helps people to feel connected to the community or other shoppers who are doing the same. Lastly, ‘competence’ - people want to feel like they are ‘smart shoppers’ and doing the right thing. Sander Van der Lindon, an assistant professor of social psychology at Cambridge University, said that a phenomenon known as ‘fear contagion’ can take hold. People’s decision making is hampered when stressed, so they follow the actions of other people. If they are panic buying, you will too.

So, can you stop people from stockpiling? Well, supermarkets can ration the amount of products consumers purchase, and governments can try to reassure people that there is no need to panic. However, it seems that it goes against our basic psychology to try and stop people from panic buying.
So, the next time a virus, natural disaster or zombie apocalypse starts, remember that panic buying is probably a given, thanks to our need for retail therapy to manage our emotional state.

vocabulary.entry: apocalypse /əˈpɒkəlɪps/ n. 末日；世界毁灭
vocabulary.example: Many movies depict the apocalypse caused by alien invasions.
vocabulary.translation: 许多电影都描绘了外星人入侵引发的末日场景。

vocabulary.entry: dystopian /dɪsˈtəʊpiən/ adj. 反乌托邦的；反面乌托邦的
vocabulary.example: The novel describes a dystopian society where freedom is restricted.
vocabulary.translation: 这本小说描绘了一个自由被限制的反乌托邦社会。

vocabulary.entry: survival /səˈvaɪvl/ n. 生存；存活
vocabulary.example: The training course teaches basic skills for survival in the wilderness.
vocabulary.translation: 这个培训课程教授野外生存的基本技能。

vocabulary.entry: quintessential /ˌkwɪntɪˈsenʃl/ adj. 典型的；精髓的
vocabulary.example: This painting is the quintessential work of the artist's early period.
vocabulary.translation: 这幅画是这位艺术家早期作品的典型代表。

vocabulary.entry: stockpile /ˈstɒkpaɪl/ v. 囤积；大量储备
vocabulary.example: People tend to stockpile necessities before a severe storm.
vocabulary.translation: 人们往往会在强风暴来临前囤积生活必需品。

vocabulary.entry: accumulate /əˈkjuːmjəleɪt/ v. 积累；积聚
vocabulary.example: It takes time to accumulate enough experience for this job.
vocabulary.translation: 要积累足够的经验来胜任这份工作需要时间。

vocabulary.entry: substantial /səbˈstænʃl/ adj. 大量的；可观的
vocabulary.example: The project received a substantial amount of funding from the government.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目从政府那里获得了大量资金支持。

vocabulary.entry: perishable /ˈperɪʃəbl/ adj. 易腐烂的；易变质的
vocabulary.example: Fruits and vegetables are perishable and need proper storage.
vocabulary.translation: 果蔬类食物容易腐烂，需要妥善储存。

vocabulary.entry: crisis /ˈkraɪsɪs/ n. 危机；危难时刻
vocabulary.example: The country is facing an economic crisis that affects everyone.
vocabulary.translation: 这个国家正面临一场影响到所有人的经济危机。

vocabulary.entry: tinned good /ˈtɪnd ɡʊd/ n. 罐装食品
vocabulary.example: Tinned good is convenient to carry during outdoor activities.
vocabulary.translation: 罐装食品在户外活动时携带很方便。

vocabulary.entry: endure /ɪnˈdjʊə(r)/ v. 持续；持久
vocabulary.example: The cold weather is expected to endure for the whole week.
vocabulary.translation: 这种寒冷的天气预计会持续整整一周。

vocabulary.entry: retail therapy /ˈriːteɪl ˈθerəpi/ n. 购物疗愈（通过购物缓解压力的方式）
vocabulary.example: She went for a bit of retail therapy after a stressful day at work.
vocabulary.translation: 在经历了一天紧张的工作后，她去购物放松了一下。

vocabulary.entry: autonomy /ɔːˈtɒnəmi/ n. 自主；自主权
vocabulary.example: The college gives students a certain degree of autonomy in choosing courses.
vocabulary.translation: 这所大学在选课方面给予学生一定的自主权。

vocabulary.entry: relatedness /rɪˈleɪtɪdnəs/ n. 关联性；归属感
vocabulary.example: The sense of relatedness is important for people's mental health.
vocabulary.translation: 归属感对人们的心理健康至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: competence /ˈkɒmpɪtəns/ n. 能力；胜任力
vocabulary.example: The manager assessed the employees' competence during the performance review.
vocabulary.translation: 经理在绩效考核期间评估了员工的工作能力。

vocabulary.entry: fear contagion /fɪə(r) kənˈteɪdʒən/ n. 恐惧传染（恐慌情绪在人群中扩散的现象）
vocabulary.example: Fear contagion can lead to irrational behavior among the public.
vocabulary.translation: 恐惧传染可能会导致公众出现非理性行为。

vocabulary.entry: hamper /ˈhæmpə(r)/ v. 阻碍；妨碍
vocabulary.example: Lack of funding will hamper the progress of the research project.
vocabulary.translation: 资金短缺会阻碍这个研究项目的进展。

vocabulary.entry: panic buying /ˈpænɪk ˈbaɪɪŋ/ n. 恐慌性抢购
vocabulary.example: Panic buying of masks happened at the start of the epidemic.
vocabulary.translation: 疫情初期出现了民众恐慌性抢购口罩的现象。

vocabulary.entry: ration /ˈræʃn/ v. 定量供应；配给
vocabulary.example: The government had to ration fuel during the energy crisis.
vocabulary.translation: 能源危机期间，政府不得不对燃油实施定量供应。

vocabulary.entry: reassure /ˌriːəˈʃʊə(r)/ v. 使安心；打消……的疑虑
vocabulary.example: The teacher tried to reassure the worried parents about their children's safety.
vocabulary.translation: 老师努力打消忧心忡忡的家长们对孩子安全的顾虑。

vocabulary.entry: given /ˈɡɪvn/ n. 必然的事；已知事实
vocabulary.example: It's a given that hard work leads to success in the long run.
vocabulary.translation: 从长远来看，努力付出就会成功，这是一个不争的事实。

vocabulary.entry: emotional state /ɪˈməʊʃənl steɪt/ n. 情绪状态
vocabulary.example: Music can have a great impact on a person's emotional state.
vocabulary.translation: 音乐对一个人的情绪状态能产生很大影响。

sentences.english: Have you ever watched one of the many TV shows set during the apocalypse - a dystopian future where life as we know it is over and people are only focussed on survival?
sentences.chinese: 你是否看过那些以末日为背景的电视剧——在反乌托邦的未来，我们熟知的生活已然终结，人们一心只想着活下去？

sentences.english: If it’s not zombies, it’s viruses or natural disasters.
sentences.chinese: 故事的导火索不是僵尸来袭，就是病毒肆虐或自然灾害爆发。

sentences.english: One thing that seems to be a quintessential part of these series is survivors searching for food and resources.
sentences.chinese: 这类剧集的一个典型特征，就是幸存者四处搜寻食物和资源。

sentences.english: Is that why people stockpile food when things go bad?
sentences.chinese: 难道这就是世道艰难时人们会囤积食物的原因吗？

sentences.english: What is stockpiling?
sentences.chinese: 什么是囤积？

sentences.english: Quite simply it’s when people accumulate a substantial number of goods, for example food or water.
sentences.chinese: 很简单，就是人们大量囤积物资，比如食物或水。

sentences.english: According to psychologist Judy Rosenberg, stockpiling perishable goods like eggs and milk is a positive sign that people believe a crisis will be over soon.
sentences.chinese: 心理学家朱迪·罗森伯格表示，囤积鸡蛋、牛奶这类易腐物资，是人们相信危机很快就会过去的积极信号。

sentences.english: When people stockpile tinned goods, it can be a sign that people fear that the crisis will endure.
sentences.chinese: 而如果囤积的是罐装食品，则可能意味着人们担心危机将会持续很长时间。

sentences.english: But why do we do it?
sentences.chinese: 但我们为什么会这么做呢？

sentences.english: Consumer psychologist Paul Marsden puts it down to three factors that relate to retail therapy.
sentences.chinese: 消费心理学家保罗·马斯登将其归结为与购物疗法相关的三个因素。

sentences.english: Firstly, ‘autonomy’ – the idea the people feel the need to be in control.
sentences.chinese: 第一是“自主掌控感”——人们会觉得自己需要掌控局面。

sentences.english: Secondly, ‘relatedness’ – panic shopping helps people to feel connected to the community or other shoppers who are doing the same.
sentences.chinese: 第二是“归属感”——恐慌性购物会让人们觉得自己和社区里的人，或是和其他同样在抢购的人产生了联结。

sentences.english: Lastly, ‘competence’ - people want to feel like they are ‘smart shoppers’ and doing the right thing.
sentences.chinese: 第三是“价值感”——人们希望自己能成为“精明的购物者”，做的事情是正确的。

sentences.english: Sander Van der Lindon, an assistant professor of social psychology at Cambridge University, said that a phenomenon known as ‘fear contagion’ can take hold.
sentences.chinese: 剑桥大学社会心理学助理教授桑德·范德林登表示，一种名为“恐惧传染”的现象可能会随之蔓延。

sentences.english: People’s decision making is hampered when stressed, so they follow the actions of other people.
sentences.chinese: 人在压力之下，决策能力会受到影响，因此会下意识模仿他人的行为。

sentences.english: If they are panic buying, you will too.
sentences.chinese: 如果别人都在恐慌性抢购，你也会跟着这么做。

sentences.english: So, can you stop people from stockpiling?
sentences.chinese: 那么，有办法阻止人们囤积物资吗？

sentences.english: Well, supermarkets can ration the amount of products consumers purchase, and governments can try to reassure people that there is no need to panic.
sentences.chinese: 超市可以对消费者的购买量进行定量供应，政府也可以努力安抚民众，让大家不必恐慌。

sentences.english: However, it seems that it goes against our basic psychology to try and stop people from panic buying.
sentences.chinese: 但事实似乎是，阻止人们进行恐慌性购物，是违背人类基本心理的。

sentences.english: So, the next time a virus, natural disaster or zombie apocalypse starts, remember that panic buying is probably a given, thanks to our need for retail therapy to manage our emotional state.
sentences.chinese: 所以下次再遇到病毒蔓延、自然灾害或是僵尸末日这样的情况时，要记住恐慌性购物或许是必然会发生的——毕竟我们需要靠购物疗愈来调节自己的情绪状态。
